title: streamline-attn-hybrid-prefetch-kv-cont-batcher
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Performance: Introduces a new lightweight hybrid attention kernel (FlashHybrid-Lite) with fused rotary/rope ops and an improved continuous-batcher plus a KV-prefetch strategy. Expected median per-token latency reduction: 12-28% across short-to-medium sequence workloads; tail p99 improvements on small-batch inference. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: Production workloads increasingly see high churn of short requests (chat turns, search reranks) where existing attention kernels pay a fixed setup cost and KV cache warms slowly. This PR introduces a compact hybrid attention kernel (FlashHybrid-Lite) that fuses rotary/rope application and elementwise postprocessing, and a scheduler + continuous-batching path that cooperates with an opportunistic KV-prefetcher. Goals: reduce p50/p95 latency for 8-512 token requests, lower token-cost by improving cache hit patterns, and stabilize tail latency under bursty traffic.

What this change does: 1) New kernel: flashhybrid_lite.{cu,cc} — a reduced-footprint attention microkernel that: applies rotary/rope on-the-fly during qk computation, emits fused qk-softmax-v matmul path with compensated fp16 accumulation, and exposes a lightweight interface for partial-KV early-return when sequence lengths are truncated. 2) Scheduler: continuous_batcher now supports "soft-window" coalescing and signals the kernel with per-batch window hints to select the short-path variant. 3) KV prefetcher: kv_prefetcher heuristic detects hot prefixes (by recent hit-rate and token-frequency) and warms the slab-backed KV cache asynchronously with bounded work per GPU. 4) Runtime integration: runtime/orchestrator ties policy flags (latency_bias, cost_bias) to pick kernel + prefetch aggressiveness. 5) Tests, benchmarks and docs: microbench harness, perf regression guardrails, and an operations note in docs/observability about tracing the prefetch events.

Testing & validation: microbench suite (suite/attn_micro) with synthetic and tokenized traces; canary run on dedicated cluster (dedicated/canary/region-us-east1) for 48h using customer-like chat workload; perf regressions monitored in CI with perf-runner. Checklist: [x] unit tests updated, [x] microbench added, [x] canary run completed, [x] documentation and config knobs added, [x] security review (no new keys), [x] SRE runbook entry created.

Compatibility notes: kernel registers a compatibility tag so older runtime can still load model variants; default policy keeps prior kernel for long-sequence heavy models. This PR is non-breaking for the API/SDK surface.

Related: builds on earlier attention scheduler work (ENG-3419) and KV cache instrumentation (ENG-3988).

Merge strategy: squash-merge to keep kernel history compact and make the canary patches obvious in the changelog.
